reviews.text: Die größte Moschee in Berlin ist ein modernes und beeindruckendes islamisches Wahrzeichen, das sich durch sein schlichtes und elegantes Design ohne Kuppel auszeichnet was sie einzigartig macht. Sie bietet großzügige Gebetsräume, die eine große Anzahl von Gläubigen aufnehmen können mit einem separaten Bereich für Frauen, der eine ruhige und angenehme Atmosphäre für das Gebet bietet. It offers spacious prayer halls that can accommodate a large number of worshippers, with a separate area for women providing a peaceful and comfortable atmosphere for prayer. In addition to religious activities, the mosque also hosts cultural events and religious classes, fostering exchange between different communities. The staff is friendly and helpful, always available to assist visitors. This mosque is an important place for spiritual reflection and education, and a perfect destination for anyone wishing to learn more about Islamic culture or to pray in a tranquil setting.

The community is friendly and warm, and the imams and staff are dedicated to the well-being of visitors. Here, you feel welcome, no matter where you come from. It's also wonderful that the mosque regularly offers events, lectures, and activities for families, children, and young people.

reviews.textTranslated:
I'm writing this review for all the women who might read it. I was at Leopoldplatz and decided to look for a mosque nearby, and this one came up in the search results. You have to get off at the Wedding station.

The mosque has a separate women's section. There are sinks and toilets, and everything was very clean. A mop is provided, so if you make a mess, please remember to clean it up yourself.

There's no bidet in the women's restroom, just a hand-held water dispenser. I think a hand-held bidet would be a better solution.

I was there around 3 p.m., and the facilities were open at that time.

reviews.text:
Allahın izniyle bugün cuma namazını orda kılmak istiyorum daha önce hiç cuma namazi kılmadım daha önce hic cematle de namaz kılmadım aslında camiye de bir iki kez gittim. Şimdi bu cami de kadınlar bölümü var mi bilmiyorum yoksa ne yapacağım onu da bilmiyorum utangaç biriyim inşallah gönlüm kırılmaz. Muhtemelen bu tecrübem iyi geçerse evim de yakın olduğu için sık sık gitmeye başlayacağım. Nasip kısmet inşallah gitmiş olursam buraya tekrar yazarım cümleten hayırlı cumalar

8 saat sonra
Kadınlar bölümü yok. Muhtemelen biliniyordu bu ki benden başka bir kadın bile yoktu cami de. Yine de beni bir odaya aldılar namaz kılmak için Allah onlardan razı olsun. Kişisel hislerime gelecek olursam olurda belki bu yorumu okurlar diye yazıyorum. Kalbim kırıldı mı, hayır ama memnun da oldum denemez bir hüzün mü desem hayal kırıklığı mı desem bunun sebebi de aslinda çok basit ilk defa cumaya giden bir kız beklediğim şey bir odada tek başına namaz kılmak değildi ama kimseyi suçlamıyorum ama keşke kadinlar için de ufak bir oda yapılsaydı. Namazi kıldım tabi çıkıp gitmekten de hemen rahatsız oldum çok fazla erkek vardı tek giriş var daha doğrusu ufak koridor var bi 10 dk bekledim cemat dağılsın diye öyle çıktım ama tabi 100 erkeğin arasında tek kadın olmak beni gerdi. Camiler herkes için Cumalar cemaatle namaz erkeklere farz tamam anlıyorum ama kadınlara da bir bölüm olmalı en azından diye düşünüyorum. Allahın" evinde "kendimi istenmeyen misafir gibi hissettim işin aslı. Yine de orda beni geri çevirmeyen beni kapıda görünce gel sana bir yer ayarlarız diyen abiye cok teşekkür ediyorum. Küçücük bir cami ama kalabalik bir cemat vardı bu da beni çok sevindirdi inşallah Müslümanların sayısı hep artarak devam eder. Yorumumu okursanız lütfen bana kızmayın ya da yanlış anlamayın ama sitemim şu özetle kadinlar da camiye rahatça gelebilsin.

Not: o kadar sorum vardı kabaliktan hissettiğim duygulardan hoca nin yanina gidip soru da soramadım hocayı da görmedim caminin içini de görmedim direk girişte ki odaya aldılar beni sagolsunlar bu da beni üzdü biraz. Ama hepinize teşekkür ederim yine de
reviews.textTranslated:
God willing, I want to pray Friday prayer there today. I've never prayed Friday prayer before, nor have I ever prayed in congregation. Actually, I've only been to a mosque once or twice. Now, I don't know if this mosque has a women's section, or what I'll do if it doesn't. I'm a shy person, I hope my feelings aren't hurt. If this experience goes well, and since my house is nearby, I'll probably start going more often. God willing, if I get the chance to go, I'll write here again. Happy Friday to everyone.

8 hours later
There's no women's section. It was probably known that there weren't any other women in the mosque besides me. Still, they took me to a room to pray. May God be pleased with them. As for my personal feelings, I'm writing this in case anyone reads this comment. Was my heart broken? No, but I can't say I was pleased either. Should I call it sadness or disappointment? The reason is actually very simple: as a girl going to Friday prayer for the first time, I didn't expect to pray alone in a room. But I'm not blaming anyone, but I wish they had made a small room for women. I prayed, but I immediately felt uncomfortable leaving. There were so many men, and there was only one entrance, or rather, a small corridor. I waited about 10 minutes for the congregation to disperse before leaving, but being the only woman among 100 men made me tense. Mosques are for everyone; Friday prayers are obligatory for men, I understand that, but I think there should be at least a separate section for women. To be honest, I felt like an unwanted guest in God's "house." Still, I want to thank the man who didn't turn me away and said, "Come, we'll find you a place," when he saw me at the door. It's a small mosque, but there was a large congregation, which made me very happy. I hope the number of Muslims continues to increase. If you read my comment, please don't get angry or misunderstand me, but my complaint is that women should be able to come to the mosque comfortably.

Note: I had so many questions, but because of the crowd and the feelings I felt, I couldn't even go to the imam to ask him, I didn't see him, and I didn't see the inside of the mosque. They took me directly to the room at the entrance, which saddened me a little. But thank you all anyway.

reviews.text:
مسجد مهما زرت مساجد، رح يضل إله مكانة مميزة بقلبي. ❤️ الأجواء فيه بشكل عام كتير حلوة ومريحة، سواء بخطبة الجمعة أو بصلاة التراويح.

وإمام المسجد الشيخ محمد رجب، ما شاء الله، مميز جداً بخطبه. أسلوبه مرتب وواضح، وحكيه واقعي وقريب من الناس، وبيخلينا نفكر كيف فينا نعين حالنا ونعيش كمسلمين مهاجرين بأوروبا ونحافظ على ديننا بنفس الوقت. بيعرف يربط المواضيع بواقعنا بطريقة جميلة ومفهومة.

كمان اختياره للمواضيع هادف، والغريب الجميل إنها أحياناً بتجي بالوقت اللي الواحد عنجد بيكون محتاج يسمعها. أسلوبه بيحبّب الإنسان بدينه وبيحنّن قلوب الناس على بعضها.

والصلاة بالمسجد إلها إحساس مميز جداً، خصوصاً بصوت الشيخ محمد رجب، ما شاء الله صوته وتلاوته فيهم خشوع كبير وبيخلّوا الواحد يعيش الصلاة من قلبه ويحس براحة وسكينة مو طبيعية.

الملاحظة الوحيدة اللي بتمنى يتم الاهتمام فيها أكتر هي نظافة سجاد المسجد، لأنه مع شوية اهتمام إضافي بالنظافة بتكون الأجواء أجمل وأريح بكتير. غير هيك الله يجزي القائمين على المسجد كل الخير على جهودهم ويبارك بالشيخ محمد رجب .
reviews.textTranslated:
No matter how many mosques I visit, this one will always hold a special place in my heart. ❤️ The atmosphere there is generally wonderful and relaxing, whether during the Friday sermon or the Taraweeh prayers.

And the imam, Sheikh Muhammad Rajab, may God bless him, is truly exceptional in his sermons. His style is organized and clear, his words are realistic and relatable, and he makes us think about how we can support ourselves and live as Muslim immigrants in Europe while preserving our faith. He knows how to connect topics to our reality in a beautiful and understandable way.

His choice of topics is also purposeful, and the beautiful thing is that sometimes they come at the exact moment when one really needs to hear them. His style endears people to their religion and softens hearts towards one another.

And praying in the mosque has a very special feeling, especially with Sheikh Muhammad Rajab's voice. May God bless him, his voice and recitation are filled with great reverence, allowing one to experience the prayer wholeheartedly and feel an extraordinary peace and tranquility.

The only thing I'd like more attention given to is the cleanliness of the mosque's carpets, because with a little extra care, the atmosphere would be much nicer and more comfortable. Otherwise, may God reward those in charge of the mosque for their efforts and bless Sheikh Muhammad Rajab.

reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Wir haben erhebliche Zweifel, ob Sie unsere Moschee überhaupt besucht haben, da das von Ihnen beschriebene Bild in keiner Weise dem tatsächlichen Charakter unserer Moschee entspricht.

Eine Moschee ist kein Restaurant oder Geschäft, das man einfach als „gut“ oder „schlecht“ bewertet. Sie ist ein Ort des Gebets und des friedlichen Zusammenlebens. Dass Menschen dort beten oder sich auf der Straße bewegen, ist kein berechtigter Grund für eine negative Bewertung.

Wenn Sie ein konkretes Problem haben, bitten wir Sie, dieses zunächst sachlich der Moscheeverwaltung mitzuteilen, bevor Sie eine solche Bewertung veröffentlichen. Pauschale und unbegründete Aussagen sind nicht hilfreich.

reviews.textTranslated: On Sunday, May 31st, they organized a party in a hall with food, outside food, and children's games. The organization was purely commercial, and you could tell they were just trying to make money. They charged three euros for adults and two euros for children. We said it was normal; it was a hall, and they have expenses, so we appreciated their efforts to make it feel like a holiday, even though they let a family of seven into the hall for free. The prices were high, but we let it slide; we don't trust each other. The cashier was selling tickets, and when we bought something, we had to pay someone. Let them sort it out amongst themselves. But then the competitions started, and they began picking their children, especially when they chose the four girls the security guards had gathered and whispered to them to participate. They asked for a nine-year-old girl, and when my daughter raised her hand, he turned away from her. May God break your heart as you broke hers! I spent 100 euros yesterday on shawarma I made at home with lettuce, and you charged me five euros! Have some consideration for these children and give them a small gift! You won expensive gifts for your group, but at least make your child guests happy. I swear to God, my daughter went home crying. I told her, "Dad, they won't let you out. They don't know me. They only let out the children they know." In the end, may God break your hearts as you broke my daughter and son's hearts yesterday. And I'll be foolish if you organize something and see my face, you Al-Furqan Mosque. I swear, if you had taken her to a church to celebrate Eid al-Adha, it would have been better than you materialistic people. She told me on the way, "Dad, I sacrificed this year and fed the meat to the poor. Why didn't God let them let me out?"

ownerDescription:
Wir arbeiten ehrenamtlich für die Berliner Community in den Bereichen Bildung, Interreligösen Dialog, Spiritualität, soziale Wohlfahrt, Interkulturelle Harmonie, Integration, Anti-Terrorismus, Anti Extremismus und globalen Frieden.
Der Pakistanischer Kulturverein Berlin Idara Minhaj-ul-Quran ist eine breit angelegte Organisation, die die wahre Vision des Islam vertritt und sich für Frieden, Liebe, Anti-Terrorismus, Bildung, interreligösen Dialog und Integration einsetzt.
Wir sind ein eingetragener Verein seit 1995.
Wir fördern die Ausbildung des klassischen Islam im zeitgenössischen Kontext. Das globale Organisationsnetzwerk Minhaj-ul-Quran International mit SItz in Lahroe, Pakistan wurde im Oktober 1980 gegründet.

reviews.name: Bey Fendi
reviews.text:
Die Mehmed Zahid Kotku Tekkesi in Berlin geht zurück auf eine Initiative des Naqschbandi-Scheichs Mehmed Zahid Kotku, der im Jahr 1965 seinen Schüler Hayrettin Özülüp Hocaefendi nach Berlin entsandte, um dort die ersten muslimischen Gläubigen spirituell zu betreuen. Zu jener Zeit gab es in Berlin noch keine Moscheen, die Muslime mussten für Freitags- und Festgebete Räume in Kirchen anmieten.

Heute setzt die Tekke die Naqschbandi-Tradition fort und bietet ein vielfältiges Programm mit spiritueller Unterweisung (irşad), religiöser Bildung, wöchentlichen Zusammenkünften, sozialen Projekten und islamisch-sufischen Lehrgesprächen.
reviews.textTranslated:
The Mehmed Zahid Kotku Tekkesi in Berlin traces its origins to an initiative of the Naqshbandi Sheikh Mehmed Zahid Kotku, who in 1965 sent his student Hayrettin Özülüp Hocaefendi to Berlin to provide spiritual guidance to the first Muslim worshippers there. At that time, there were no mosques in Berlin; Muslims had to rent rooms in churches for Friday and festival prayers.

Today, the tekke continues the Naqshbandi tradition and offers a diverse program including spiritual instruction (irşad), religious education, weekly gatherings, social projects, and Islamic-Sufi discussions.
